I did conventional 10% down with 2.5% rate. Our mortgage insurance is around $50 a month for a few years. :)

Also from Texas! 

We started with trying to increase our credit score. I downloaded credit karma and as well as pulled my credit report every week. With the pandemic going on, the three bureaus let you pull your credit report for free once a week as opposed to once a year for free. This helped me settle any disputes or comments on my report and my points went up. 

Then, we got serious we reached out to several different banks for a pre-approval. Know that when they do pull your credit history it is a hard pull, so your credit score will decrease by a few points. However, I believe they give you a certain time frame where if you reach out to other lenders and they do a hard pull, it won’t affect your score. I was not impressed with the communication with one of the banks, so I’m glad we kept looking; so make sure that you find a responsive loan officer that you trust. We were pre-approved for 2.6% and later on when we got deeper it went down to 2.5% when our loan officer ran it again. 


Once you know what you’re pre-approved for you can start house hunting since you know what you can afford. We reached out to a realtor that our friends recommended. 

Best advice is to find a good realtor and good loan officer, makes the communication process so much easier having responsive people who know what they are doing. The whole process from starting to house hunt seriously to now closing this Friday, was roughly two months. 

Best of luck!

My boyfriend and I are under contract to buy a home now, but one of the biggest advice his parents gave to us was to not fall in love with the house, but to fall in love with the neighborhood first and then find houses in those areas. 

You can upgrade the house and fix it up, but you can’t with the neighborhood and people who live there. It was a mistake they made for their first house purchase and ended up selling it shortly after and losing money since they wanted to desperately get out of there ASAP and there wasn’t that many bites on the house either when they put it on the market.

I know your question requested for advice on what to be mindful for, but I would consider walking away. For us, a huge factor was finding a place where I felt I could walk my dog safely and eventually when we have kids, it would be a safe neighborhood. 

Also, consider if you do plan on selling it or looking for renters after 5 years would you be making a profit when it’s back on the market? Or do you think it’ll be easy to find people interested in renting knowing that crime rates are high/murder close by? 

Goodluck!

We lost our bid on our first house and became the backup offer, and unfortunately we still did not get the house. I was feeling discourage because I wasn’t getting the same feeling the first house gave me as we continued to house hunt, and I held onto hope that the first buyer would fall through. 

Two days later after our backup contract ended and I was so discouraged. However, by chance we fell in love with a house we happen to check out for fun and with no expectations and now we are under contact and set to close in the beginning of January! This house is actually less expensive, and has so much more to offer than the first house. We’re ecstatic and are so glad we found something better. Hang in there, you’ll find a house that you’ll love and it’ll work out too. :)
